# Preprocessing, clustering, and PCA

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-reference.swift from the Quiver 1.6.0 public API. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every API below exists in Quiver 1.0.0 and later unless it is tagged *(since X)*. Each entry is the declaration, then the first line of its documentation.

## Transformer

`protocol Transformer : Sendable` — A fitted preprocessing stage that maps a feature matrix to a new one. *(since 1.6.0)*

- `func transform(_ features: [[Double]]) -> [[Double]]` — Transforms a feature matrix using the parameters learned at fit time. Returns: The transformed matrix, one output row per input row. *(since 1.6.0)*

## Pipeline

`struct Pipeline<Model> where Model : Decodable, Model : Encodable, Model : Equatable, Model : Sendable` — A matched pair of scaler and model that travel together. *(since 1.1.0)*

Conforms to: Codable, Equatable.

- `let scaler: StandardScaler` — The scaler that normalizes raw inputs before prediction. *(since 1.1.0)*
- `let reducer: PCA?` — The optional dimensionality-reduction stage applied after scaling. *(since 1.6.0)*
- `let model: Model` — The trained model that produces predictions from transformed features. *(since 1.1.0)*
- `init(scaler: StandardScaler, reducer: PCA? = nil, model: Model)` — Creates a pipeline from a fitted scaler, an optional reducer, and a trained model. *(since 1.6.0)*
- `func predict(_ features: [[Double]]) -> [Int]` — Scales raw features, applies the reducer when present, and predicts class labels in one call. Returns: Predicted class labels, one per sample. *(since 1.1.0)*
- `func predict(_ features: [[Double]]) -> [Double]` — Scales raw features, applies the reducer when present, and predicts continuous values in one call. Returns: Predicted values, one per sample. *(since 1.1.0)*
- `static func fit(features: [[Double]], labels: [Int], k: Int = 3, metric: DistanceMetric = .euclidean, weight: VoteWeight = .uniform) -> Pipeline<KNearestNeighbors>` — Fits a scaler, trains a K-Nearest Neighbors classifier, and bundles them into a Pipeline. Returns: An immutable `Pipeline<KNearestNeighbors>`. *(since 1.1.0)*
- `static func fit(features: [[Double]], labels: [Int], componentCount: Int, k: Int = 3, metric: DistanceMetric = .euclidean, weight: VoteWeight = .uniform) -> Pipeline<KNearestNeighbors>` — Fits a scaler, projects the scaled features onto principal components, trains a K-Nearest Neighbors classifier on the projection, and bundles all three into a Pipeline. Returns: An immutable `Pipeline<KNearestNeighbors>` carrying the scaler, the fitted reducer, and the trained classifier. *(since 1.6.0)*
- `static func fit(features: [[Double]], labels: [Int]) -> Pipeline<GaussianNaiveBayes>` — Fits a scaler, trains a Gaussian Naive Bayes classifier, and bundles them into a Pipeline. Returns: An immutable `Pipeline<GaussianNaiveBayes>`. *(since 1.1.0)*
- `static func fit(data: [[Double]], k: Int, maxIterations: Int = 100, seed: UInt64? = nil) -> Pipeline<KMeans>` — Fits a scaler, trains a K-Means clustering model, and bundles them into a Pipeline. Returns: An immutable `Pipeline<KMeans>`. *(since 1.1.0)*
- `static func fit(features: [[Double]], targets: [Double], intercept: Bool = true) throws -> Pipeline<LinearRegression>` — Fits a scaler, trains a Linear Regression model, and bundles them into a Pipeline. Returns: An immutable `Pipeline<LinearRegression>`. Throws: `MatrixError.singular` if features are linearly dependent. *(since 1.1.0)*
- `static func fit(features: [[Double]], targets: [Double], learningRate: Double = 0.01, maxIterations: Int = 1000, tolerance: Double = 1.0e-6, intercept: Bool = true) throws -> Pipeline<GradientDescent>` — Fits a scaler, trains a gradient descent regressor, and bundles them into a Pipeline. Returns: An immutable `Pipeline<GradientDescent>`. Throws: `GradientDescentError` on divergence. *(since 1.4.0)*
- `static func fit(features: [[Double]], labels: [Int], learningRate: Double = 0.01, maxIterations: Int = 1000, tolerance: Double = 1.0e-6, intercept: Bool = true) throws -> Pipeline<LogisticRegression>` — Fits a scaler, trains a logistic regression classifier, and bundles them into a Pipeline. Returns: An immutable `Pipeline<LogisticRegression>`. Throws: `GradientDescentError` on divergence. *(since 1.4.0)*

## StandardScaler

`struct StandardScaler` — A column-wise z-score scaler for feature matrices. *(since 1.1.0)*

Conforms to: Codable, Equatable, Transformer.

- `let means: [Double]` — Per-column mean values learned from the training data. *(since 1.1.0)*
- `let stds: [Double]` — Per-column standard deviation values learned from the training data. *(since 1.1.0)*
- `let featureCount: Int` — Number of feature columns the scaler was fitted on. *(since 1.1.0)*
- `static func fit(features: [[Double]]) -> StandardScaler` — Learns column-wise mean and standard deviation from a feature matrix. Returns: A fitted `StandardScaler` ready to transform data. *(since 1.1.0)*
- `func transform(_ features: [[Double]]) -> [[Double]]` — Scales a feature matrix using the learned column statistics. Returns: A z-scored copy of the input matrix. *(since 1.1.0)*

## FeatureScaler

`struct FeatureScaler` — A column-wise min-max scaler for feature matrices.

Conforms to: Codable, Equatable.

- `let minimums: [Double]` — Per-column minimum values learned from the training data.
- `let maximums: [Double]` — Per-column maximum values learned from the training data.
- `let range: ClosedRange<Double>` — The target range that scaled values are mapped to.
- `let featureCount: Int` — Number of feature columns the scaler was fitted on.
- `static func fit(features: [[Double]], range: ClosedRange<Double> = 0.0...1.0) -> FeatureScaler` — Learns column-wise min and max values from a feature matrix. Returns: A fitted `FeatureScaler` ready to transform data.
- `func transform(_ features: [[Double]]) -> [[Double]]` — Scales a feature matrix using the learned column statistics. Returns: A scaled copy of the input matrix.

## KMeans

`struct KMeans` — A trained K-Means clustering model.

Conforms to: Codable, Equatable.

- `let centroids: [[Double]]` — The final centroid positions after convergence.
- `let labels: [Int]` — The cluster label assigned to each training sample (0 to k-1).
- `let inertia: Double` — Sum of squared distances from each point to its assigned centroid.
- `let iterations: Int` — The number of iterations the algorithm ran before stopping.
- `let featureCount: Int` — Number of features the model was trained on.
- `static func fit(data: [[Double]], k: Int, maxIterations: Int = 100, seed: UInt64? = nil) -> KMeans` — Fits a K-Means model to the given data. Returns: A trained `KMeans` model with final centroids and cluster assignments.
- `static func bestFit(data: [[Double]], k: Int, maxIterations: Int = 100, attempts: Int = 10) -> KMeans` — Fits multiple K-Means models with different seeds and returns the best one. Returns: The `KMeans` model with the lowest inertia across all attempts.
- `static func elbowMethod(data: [[Double]], kRange: ClosedRange<Int>, maxIterations: Int = 100, seed: UInt64? = nil) -> [(k: Int, inertia: Double)]` — Computes inertia for a range of k values (elbow method). Returns: An array of (k, inertia) tuples, one per k value.
- `func clusters(from data: [[Double]]) -> [Cluster]` — Groups the original training data into clusters with their centroids. Returns: An array of `Cluster` values, one per centroid, in centroid order.
- `func predict(_ data: [[Double]]) -> [Int]` — Assigns cluster labels to new data points based on the trained centroids. Returns: An array of cluster labels (0 to k-1), one per sample.

## Cluster

`struct Cluster` — A single cluster from a K-Means model, containing a centroid and its assigned data points.

Conforms to: Codable, Equatable, Sequence.

- `let centroid: [Double]` — The centroid position for this cluster.
- `let points: [[Double]]` — The data points assigned to this cluster.
- `var count: Int { get }` — The number of data points in this cluster.
- `func makeIterator() -> IndexingIterator<[[Double]]>` — Returns an iterator over the data points in this cluster.

## PCA

`struct PCA` — A dimensionality-reduction transformer that projects features onto the directions of largest variance. *(since 1.6.0)*

Conforms to: Codable, Equatable, Transformer.

- `let components: [[Double]]` — The principal components, one per row — a (componentCount × featureCount) matrix. With three input features and two components requested, `components` has two rows of three values, and `components[0]` is the direction of largest variance. Each row is a unit vector, sign-fixed so its largest-magnitude element is positive. *(since 1.6.0)*
- `let means: [Double]` — Per-feature mean values learned from the training data. *(since 1.6.0)*
- `let explainedVariances: [Double]` — The variance captured by each retained component, largest first. *(since 1.6.0)*
- `let explainedVarianceRatios: [Double]` — The fraction of total variance captured by each retained component. The values sum to 1.0 only when every component is retained (`componentCount == featureCount`); with fewer components the sum is the fraction of variance the projection keeps. *(since 1.6.0)*
- `let componentCount: Int` — Number of principal components the model retains. *(since 1.6.0)*
- `let featureCount: Int` — Number of feature columns the model was fitted on. *(since 1.6.0)*
- `static func fit(features: [[Double]], componentCount: Int) -> PCA` — Learns principal components from a feature matrix. Returns: A fitted `PCA` ready to transform data. *(since 1.6.0)*
- `func transform(_ features: [[Double]]) -> [[Double]]` — Projects a feature matrix onto the principal components. Returns: The projected matrix, one row per sample. *(since 1.6.0)*
- `func inverseTransform(_ projected: [[Double]]) -> [[Double]]` — Maps projected data back into the original feature space. Returns: The reconstructed matrix in the original feature space. *(since 1.6.0)*
